A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GNVC-VD paper, with 16 complete pages including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content apart from the page-1 arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original GNVC-VD benchmark results and ablations in Section 4, plus temporal-consistency measurements, runtime results, and a user study in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, ablation, runtime, and user-study results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical contextual latent codec, VideoDiT flow-matching refinement, conditioning adapters, training objectives, and two-stage training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Vimeo-90k and longer original Vimeo sequences and evaluate video compression on HEVC-B, UVG, and MCL-JCV. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments: HEVC, VVC, DCVC-FM, DCVC-RT, PLVC, and GLC-Video remain in the rate–distortion comparisons. The temporal-comparison and user-study comparator sets also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same training schedules, 96-frame RGB evaluations, preprocessing, GOP configurations, and metrics. Appendix C.4 retains the same randomized pairwise user-study procedure.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains identical ablations removing latent refinement, Stage I loss, or Stage II loss. Appendix C's temporal analyses, complexity measurements, user study, and qualitative examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including the user-study preference percentages. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted curves, and qualitative examples match, including Tables 2–7 and the appendix results. For example, Figure 10 retains preference rates of 87.5%, 85.0%, 88.8%, and 98.8% against the same four baselines.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, flow-matching formulation, velocity derivation, and Equations (1)–(12) are identical. The appendices contain no changed theoretical material.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claims about video-native diffusion for sequence-level compression and refinement, and the same claims of improved perceptual quality and reduced flickering at ultra-low bitrates.

C2.justification: Interpretations of temporal coherence, oversmoothing, latent alignment, and pixel-level adaptation are identical. The qualifications concerning distortion metrics and the need for more efficient coding and refinement also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–C retain the same hyperparameters, hardware, codec settings, architecture details, parameter counts, timing information, and baseline-access links.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 55 reference entries are unchanged. The positioning relative to image-prior codecs such as GLC-Video and DiffVC and to video diffusion models remains identical.

P1.justification: Only the page-1 arXiv margin stamp changes from v1, dated 4 December 2025, to v2, dated 23 February 2026. The prose, terminology, headings, and section organization are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–7 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the sole visible difference is the version/date stamp assessed under P1.

improvement.justification: The main text and appendices retain identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, and presentation. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp neither resolves a deficiency nor changes the paper's overall quality.
